items.statement:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with no imaginary simple roots, so $a_{ii}=2$, and put $b_{ij}:=d_i\,a_{ij}=(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)$, a symmetric matrix with $b_{ii}=2d_i>0$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]], [[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix a field $k$. A **KLR datum** on it is a family $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i
e j}$ of polynomials $Q_{ij}\in k[u,v]$ such that

(Q1) $Q_{ij}
e0$ for $i
e j$ and $Q_{ii}:=0$;

(Q2) $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$ for all $i
e j$;

(Q3) $Q_{ij}$ is homogeneous of total degree $-2b_{ij}$ for the degree assignments $\deg u:=2d_i$, $\deg v:=2d_j$;

(Q4) the two extremal coefficients of $Q_{ij}$, namely that of $u^{-a_{ij}}$ and that of $v^{-a_{ji}}$, are nonzero.

For a chosen finite quiver with a compatible automorphism having no arrow within a vertex orbit, write $i\cdot j=b_{ij}$ and let $d_{ij}$ be the number of arrow orbits directed from vertex orbit $i$ to vertex orbit $j$; the specialization applies when its induced Cartan datum is the fixed one. items.strategy:
**Well-definedness.** $R_n(Q)$ is defined as the quotient of the free unital associative $k$-algebra on the symbols $e(
u)$ ($
u\in I^n$), $x_a$, $	au_a$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the displayed relations, so no existence issue arises. Two points deserve record. First, relation (7) is stated as an equality in $k[x_a,x_{a+1},x_{a+2}]e(
u)$: writing $Q(u,v)=\sum_a u^a q_a(v)$, the difference $Q(u,v)-Q(w,v)=\sum_a(u^a-w^a)q_a(v)$ is divisible by $u-w$ in the polynomial ring, and its quotient evaluated at $(u,w)=(x_a,x_{a+2})$, $v=x_{a+1}$ gives the displayed correction; the special case $a_{ij}=0$ with $Q_{ij}$ a nonzero constant is included, where the correction vanishes and the ordinary braid relation holds on $
u_a=
u_{a+2}$. Second, the mixed relations are word-component identities: the final $e(
u)$ is essential, since a global dot commutator has different components on equal and unequal colors. On an equal-color component they are the identities $\partial_ax_a-x_{a+1}\partial_a=1$ and $\partial_ax_{a+1}-x_a\partial_a=-1$ for $\partial_a=(1-s_a)/(x_a-x_{a+1})$. The two global sign conventions for $	au_a$ are exchanged by $	au_a\mapsto-	au_a$, which preserves (4) and flips the signs in (6) and (7); this page fixes the convention of (6) once and for all and every later item uses it.

**Choice.** The definitional clauses are choice-free: they name a presented algebra and its weight decomposition over a fixed datum, with no selection of representatives or of auxiliary sets.

items.title: Induction and restriction bimodules for KLR algebras
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ put $e( eta,\gamma):=\sum_{
u\in I^{ eta},
u'\in I^{\gamma}}e(
u\ast
u')\in R( eta+\gamma)$, where $
u\ast
u'$ is concatenation; this is an idempotent. The block inclusions $R( eta)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $r\mapsto r\otimes1$ and $R(\gamma)\hookrightarrow R( eta+\gamma)$, $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ combine into an injective $k$-algebra map $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)	o R( eta+\gamma)$ whose image is the separated-block subalgebra of the corner $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$; the inclusion generally is proper; in the diagram calculus it is horizontal concatenation of diagrams. **Induction** and **restriction** are the functors on graded left modules
$$\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N):=R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}(M\otimes_kN),\qquad \mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L:=e( eta,\gamma)L,$$
where $\otimes_{R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)}$ is the graded balanced tensor product of [[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] (total-degree grading) and $M\otimes_kN$ carries the graded tensor product structure; $\mathrm{Ind}$ is a functor on graded modules over the graded algebra $R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$ (through the tensor product of the two graded modules) and, since $R( eta+\gamma)e( eta,\gamma)$ is a graded $(R( eta+\gamma),R( eta)\otimes_kR(\gamma))$-bimodule and $e( eta,\gamma)R( eta+\gamma)$ is its right-module counterpart, the two tensor functors are of the two sidedness types of [[thm-graded-bimodule-tensor-hom-adjunction]]. Both functors are additive and degree-zero on degree-zero maps and extend to the direct sums over weights. Shifts satisfy $\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M\{r\} oxtimes N\{s\})\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{ eta,\gamma}(M oxtimes N)\{r+s\}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}(L\{r\})\cong(\mathrm{Res}_{ eta,\gamma}L)\{r\}$ ([[lem-graded-balanced-tensor-and-shift-isomorphisms]]). For a partial flag $ eta= eta_1+\cdots+ eta_r$ the iterated functors are defined by iteration, and the parenthesization-independent identification is the one consumed below.
items.strategy: Concatenation sends the two tensor-factor identities to e(beta,gamma), so this is a unital map into that corner, not a unital map into all of R(beta+gamma) unless e=1. Relations within each block are preserved and separated generators commute; this defines the homomorphism. The PBW monomials with permutations contained in S_|beta| x S_|gamma| and arbitrary dots are exactly the images of tensor products of the two PBW bases, so they are independent. Hence the map is injective. Its image need not equal the corner: for beta=gamma=alpha_i the corner is NH_2 while its image is k[x_1,x_2], excluding tau_1. Balanced tensor and idempotent multiplication now give the displayed functors. Each balance relation and outer action preserves degree, and moving shifts through the total tensor grading gives the two stated shift isomorphisms. Iterating block concatenation gives the same idempotent and multiplication map in every parenthesization; the map a tensor (b tensor m) -> ab tensor m and its inverse on balanced tensors prove the associativity identification. No AC is used.

items.title: Nil-Hecke idempotents and divided-power KLR projectives
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.
items.strategy:
**Nil-Hecke matrix calculation.** Put $V=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $C=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]=V^{S_n}$ and $N=\binom n2$. The elementary symmetric functions are algebraically independent and generate the symmetric ring: subtracting the leading symmetric monomial orbit successively expresses every invariant as a polynomial in them, and their distinct leading monomials give independence. Adjoin $x_1$ as a root of the monic polynomial $T^n-e_1T^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n$, then $x_2$ as a root of its quotient by $T-x_1$, and continue. Eliminating coefficients recovers the polynomial ring in the roots; each monic extension is free on powers below its degree. Hence $V$ is free over $C$ on $x^a$ with $0\le a_r\le n-r$.

Write $\delta=(n-1,n-2,\ldots,0)$. Expanding the divided differences gives $\partial_{w_0}(f)=\sum_{w\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(w)w(f)/\prod_{a<b}(x_a-x_b)$: the braid relations make this independent of the reduced word, and the numerator of $x^\delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. Thus $\partial_{w_0}(x^\delta)=1$, its values are symmetric, and it kills every other Artin basis monomial by degree. It is therefore the coefficient-of-$x^\delta$ trace of the monic tower. This trace has a perfect $C$-bilinear pairing $\langle f,g\rangle=\partial_{w_0}(fg)$: for a monic extension of degree $m$, the coefficient-of-$T^{m-1}$ trace has matrix zero below the antidiagonal and ones on it in the power basis, hence determinant $\pm1$; composing these perfect trace pairings through the tower preserves perfection. Choose the finite trace-dual Artin basis $(b_a^*)$ to $(b_a)$. The operators $f\mapsto b_a\partial_{w_0}(b_b^*f)$ are matrix units, all lying in $NH_n$; faithfulness of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] therefore identifies $NH_n=\operatorname{End}_C(V)$ in every characteristic.

**Idempotents, column and duality.** In this faithful action, $E=\partial_{w_0}x^\delta$ sends $f$ to $\partial_{w_0}(x^\delta f)\in C$ and fixes $C$, so $E^2=E$. Reflection $\psi$ fixes dots and crossings and reverses products, giving $e_{i,n}=\psi(E)$ also idempotent and nonzero. Both have degree zero. The map $NH_nE\to V$, $aE\mapsto a(1)$, is an isomorphism with inverse $f\mapsto m_fE$: $E$ is the rank-one projection onto $C\cdot1$, so $aE=m_{a(1)}E$. Its endomorphism ring is $C$ and its degree-zero part is $k$, proving graded indecomposability. The trace pairing has degree $-2d_iN$ and satisfies $\langle af,g\rangle=\langle f,\psi(a)g\rangle$: this is immediate for dots and follows for $\partial_r$ by expanding $(1-s_r)/(x_r-x_{r+1})$ in the trace formula. Consequently $V^\#\cong V\{-2d_iN\}$, and $P_{i,n}=V\{-d_iN\}$ is self-dual. The Artin basis degrees yield $NH_n\cong\bigoplus_a V\{-2d_i|a|\}$, since $\operatorname{End}_C(V)=V\otimes_C V^*$; centering gives multiplicity $q_i^N\prod_{m=1}^n(1+q_i^{-2}+\cdots+q_i^{-2(m-1)})=[n]_i!$. This also proves uniqueness of the indecomposable projective shift orbit: a finite graded projective over the connected positively graded ring $C$ is shifted-free, by lifting a basis modulo $C^+$ and using its projective splitting and the least-degree argument on kernel and cokernel, and the matrix equivalence transports that assertion to $NH_n$.

**Duality and induction.** For a finite graded projective $B=R(\beta)\otimes R(\gamma)$-module $M$, finite-projective evaluation gives $\operatorname{HOM}_R(Re\otimes_BM,R)\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,eR)\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,B)\otimes_BeR$. Twisting by reflection yields $(\operatorname{Ind}M)^\#\cong\operatorname{Ind}(M^\#)$ with the same block order and grading. The identities are checked on finite shifted-free $M$ and then its summands. Thus ordered inductions of the normalized one-color columns are self-dual, as required for bar compatibility.

**Two colours and order.** For several colours $P_\theta$ is defined by induction along the ordered blocks, so the class is the ordered induction product; blocks of orthogonal colors commute by the invertible degree-zero block shuffle, since their $Q_{ij}$ are nonzero constants, while adjacent colours are related only by the Serre relations proved later on this page, so no silent symmetrization of the word $\theta$ is made. The construction selects no representatives beyond the fixed reduced-expression system of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] and uses no choice principle.

items.title: Graded Krull-Schmidt and shift-orbit bases for finitely generated KLR modules
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; establish freeness over the central color-symmetric subalgebra, then Krull-Schmidt and projective covers by finite-dimensional endomorphism-algebra arguments, then the orbit bases.

1.1 (Central polynomial subalgebra and freeness.) Let $C_\beta$ be the color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra: on the summand $e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\nu)$ it is the polynomial ring in the elementary symmetric functions of the dots of each color separately. It is central: unequal crossings permute dot positions, and equal-color divided differences $\partial_a$ commute with symmetric polynomials in $x_a,x_{a+1}$ by the Leibniz rule $\partial_a(fg)=\partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)\partial_a(g)$ applied to $s_a$-invariant $f$. In each constant-color block of length $m$ the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ is free over the symmetric subring on the Artin monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_m^{a_m}$, $0\le a_r\le m-r$: adjoining the first root of the universal polynomial $T^m-e_1T^{m-1}+\cdots+(-1)^me_m$ presents $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ as a free rank-$m$ module over the coefficient ring, the corresponding quotient of $T^m-\cdots$ by $T-x_1$ is monic of degree $m-1$ with the correct coefficients, and iteration gives those monomials as a basis while the elementary symmetric functions of the roots recover the $e_r$. Combining with the PBW basis [F1], whose dot monomials factor over the color blocks, gives that $R(\beta)$ is a finite free $C_\beta$-module, of rank $(|\beta|!)^2$ per weight counting the permutation basis; only centrality and this freeness are used below. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 (Krull-Schmidt and splitting.) Every finitely generated graded module is bounded below and locally finite by [F1]. Choose finitely many homogeneous generators of degrees $d_j$; evaluation on the generators injects $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ into the finite product of the finitely many finite-dimensional pieces $M_{d_j}$, so every degree-zero endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional, and a nontrivial homogeneous idempotent splits $M$ into two nonzero summands with strictly smaller endomorphism algebras; splitting terminates. For an indecomposable $M$, every endomorphism $f$ satisfies a polynomial minimal equation because $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ is finite-dimensional; factoring it as $T^rg(T)$ with $g(0)\ne0$, Bezout gives a polynomial projector separating the nilpotent part from the invertible part, so indecomposability forces $f$ or $1-f$ to be invertible. Hence the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal, and the usual comparison of two decompositions $\bigoplus p_ii_jp_j=\mathrm{id}$ produces a matching summand and cancellation, proving uniqueness in the degree-zero category; the shifts are recorded as part of each summand. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 (Simples and covers.) For a graded simple $S$ and a positive-degree central $c\in C_\beta^+$, the kernel and image of $c$ are graded submodules; if $c$ acted nontrivially it would be injective and hence surjective, contradicting the least nonzero degree of the bounded-below module $S$; so $C_\beta^+S=0$ and $S$ is finite-dimensional because $\bar R=R(\beta)/C_\beta^+R(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional by step 1.1. The finite-dimensional basis theorem [F3] applies to $\bar R$: it has finitely many graded simple shift orbits, and the same then holds for $R(\beta)$, since any simple $R(\beta)$-module is one. Projective covers are then lifted to $R(\beta)$: choose a finite shifted-free $R$-module $F$ whose reduction $\bar F$ surjects onto the projective cover $\bar Q\twoheadrightarrow\bar S$. That surjection splits by projectivity of $\bar Q$, giving an idempotent of $\operatorname{End}^0_{\bar R}(\bar F)$; entrywise reduction $\operatorname{End}^0_R(F)\to\operatorname{End}^0_{\bar R}(\bar F)$ is surjective; the reduction kernel in $\operatorname{End}^0_R(F)$ is nilpotent because its entries have positive central degree and a long product has degree exceeding every fixed difference of generator degrees minus the lower bound of $F$, so the projector onto $\bar Q$ is lifted by the finite nilpotent-ideal idempotent-lifting iteration $e\mapsto e-(2e-1)(e^2-e)$; the image $Q$ of the lifted projector is projective, its kernel is graded superfluous (after reduction by $C^+$ it is superfluous for $\bar Q$, and a bounded-below graded quotient $X=C^+X$ vanishes by its least nonzero degree), so $Q$ is an indecomposable projective cover, and every indecomposable projective is such a cover up to shift. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 (Orbit bases.) Finite decompositions into indecomposables give that $K_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of indecomposable finite graded projectives, with $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$, and finite length of finite-dimensional modules gives that $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the simple shift orbits; both are $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-modules in the sense of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], the shift action is free because a nonzero finite-dimensional graded module is not isomorphic to a nonzero shift of itself (compare its least and greatest degrees), and the finite-dimensional theorem [F3] gives the same statement for the quotient categories. For a projective cover $P_b$ and simple $S_c$ with their selected shifts, $\operatorname{Hom}(P_b,S_c)=0$ unless $b=c$ at the selected shift, when it equals $\operatorname{End}(S_b)$ by the uniqueness of the cover, whose degree-zero endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra by Schur's argument; finite-dimensionality alone does not identify it with $k$; this is the diagonal-entry computation of the Hom pairing of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]. The stronger statement that the diagonal scalar rings equal $k$ over every field, and the associated unscaled dual-basis conclusion, are not inferred here from finite-dimensional algebra alone and are proved separately later on this page; nothing above uses them. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, algebra] ∎

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction adjunctions preserve projectives
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; decompose $Ae$ as a right block module and $eA$ as a left block module, then establish exactness, projectivity, adjunctions and the double-coset filtration.

1.1 (Shuffle decomposition and freeness.) Choose reduced PBW words adapted to the parabolic subgroup $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$. For each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ and minimal right coset representative $w$, the vectors $\tau_we(\xi)b$, with $b$ ranging through the PBW basis of $e(\xi)B$, form precisely the PBW basis of the right $B$-module $Ae$: the permutation is a minimal shuffle followed by an internal block permutation, with additive length, and the right idempotent records the source word in the corner $e$. Thus $Ae\cong\bigoplus_{w,\xi}e(\xi)B\{\delta_R(w,\xi)\}$, with the displayed degree of $\tau_we(\xi)$. Reversal of products fixing dots, crossings and idempotents preserves the defining relations and is an anti-involution; it sends $Ae$ to $eA$ and $\tau_we(\xi)$ to $e(\xi)\tau_{w^{-1}}$, giving the left $B$-module decomposition of $eA$ into the corresponding $Be(\xi)$ with shifts $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)$. Both decompositions are finite sums of principal graded projectives. Ungraded, for each shuffle the sum over all concatenated $\xi$ is one copy of $B$, so both ranks are $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. Neither bimodule is replaced by $eAe$: its unconstrained opposite endpoint is essential for the shuffle basis. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 (Left adjunction.) For a graded left $B$-module $X$ and a graded left $A$-module $L$, currying gives the natural degree-zero bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(Ae\otimes_BX,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(X,eL)$, $\Phi\mapsto(x\mapsto\Phi(e\otimes x))$, with inverse $f\mapsto(ae\otimes x\mapsto a\,f(x))$, well defined on balanced tensors and inverse by the idempotence of $e$; this is the adjunction of [F3] for the $(A,B)$-bimodule $Ae$. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 (Exactness and projectivity.) The right $B$-module $Ae$ is projective, hence flat, by step 1.1, so $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ is exact by [F2]. Idempotent restriction is exact on left modules: for a surjection $L\to N$, a vector $en\in eN$ lifts to $e\ell\in eL$, and kernels and images commute with multiplication by the degree-zero idempotent $e$; no right action on $L$ is required. A finitely generated graded projective left $B$-module is a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $B$, so its induction is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $Ae$. As a left $A$-module $Ae$ is the image of the degree-zero idempotent endomorphism $a\mapsto ae$ of $A$, hence is finitely generated graded projective. Similarly, if $P$ is a finitely generated graded projective left $A$-module, realize $P$ as a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $A$ and apply $e(-)$ to its split inclusion and projection. Then $eP$ is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $eA$, which is finitely generated graded projective as a left $B$-module by step 1.1. Internal shifts commute with induction and restriction because their balance relations and idempotent action have degree zero. This proves exactness, shift compatibility and both finite-projective preservation clauses. [step 1.1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.2 (Coinduction and the longest shuffle.) The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$ by [F3] applied to $M=eA$, and explicit currying gives $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$. For the second-adjunction formula let $y$ be the longest block shuffle of the two blocks, of degree $-c$ (each of the $|\beta||\gamma|$ crossed positions contributes the negative pairing of the two colours), and let $e'=e(\gamma,\beta)$ be the reversed-block idempotent. By PBW there is a well-defined $B$-balanced coefficient map $t:eAe'\to B$ projecting onto the $y$-coefficient, where the reversed block order is read in $B$ through the flip equivalence $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)\to R(\gamma)\otimes_kR(\beta)$; dot slides and block crossings preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient, while every dot or braid correction in a shorter shuffle has strictly smaller shuffle length and is killed by $t$. Hence the map $\Phi:Ae'\to\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)$, $z\mapsto(u\mapsto t(uz))$, is a degree-$c$ map of $(A,B)$-bimodules, and it is compatible with the flip identification. [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

2.3 (Mackey filtration.) Fix a second flag with idempotent $e'=e(\beta',\gamma')$ and choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row block permutation group and the column block permutation group acting on the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ positions. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner $eAe'$ by the four intersection blocks $(a,b;c,d)$ with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, and filter by the crossing length of the double-coset representatives. The span of the double cosets of strictly smaller length is a $(B,B')$-sub-bimodule: sliding a block generator across a representative either stays in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or produces a quadratic/braid correction of strictly smaller length, which lies in the smaller span. In the associated quotient only the monomials whose permutation is the minimal double-coset representative survive; they are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases of the four blocks composed with the row and column induced bimodules and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks, which carries the shift $-(b\mid c)$ because the crossed colours are precisely $b$ and $c$. The basis bijection defines inverse maps between the associated quotient and the composite four-block restriction/induction bimodule, so the filtration is proved and not merely a character identity; iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block statement. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 (Triangularity and the functor formula.) Pair the right $B$-module shuffle basis of $Ae'$ (through the block flip) with the left $B$-module shuffle basis of $eA$ by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, the coefficient matrix of the pairing $u\mapsto t(uz)$ is triangular: a complementary pair is exactly the reduced longest shuffle with coefficient $1$ up to the absorbed equal-colour signs, and a noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic or braid correction to strictly smaller length, hence vanishes in the associated graded. Finite triangular elimination over $B$ (division by the diagonal units $1$) inverts the matrix, so $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of graded $(A,B)$-bimodules; consequently $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\cong Ae'\{c\}$ with the $B$-action transported by the block flip. Since $eA$ is finite projective over $B$ by step 1.1, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\otimes_BX\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,X)$ for every graded $B$-module $X$ (checked on finite free modules and finite summands), and tracking the outer right $B$-action through the flip gives the functorial isomorphism $\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}$. [step 2.2, F1, F3, algebra]

4.1 All clauses of the statement are now proved: step 1.1 gives the freeness and the labelled shuffle shifts, step 2.1 the exactness, shift compatibility and projective preservation, step 1.2 the left adjunction, steps 2.2 and 3.1 the right adjoint and its exact reversed-block formula, and step 2.3 the finite Mackey filtration and its multi-block version. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 2.3, algebra] ∎

items.title: The KLR Cartan (graded Hom) pairing on the projective Grothendieck group
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finitely generated graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.
items.strategy:
**Well-definedness.** $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a graded $k$-vector space of finite dimension in each degree and bounded below, so its graded dimension is a well-defined element of $\mathbb Z((q))$; freeness of $R(\beta)$ over the central subalgebra $C_\beta$ ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]) and the fact that every finite graded projective is a direct summand of a finite shifted free module upgrade the value to $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$: lifting a homogeneous $k$-basis of $V/C_\beta^+V$ gives a surjection from a finite shifted free $C_\beta$-module with vanishing cokernel, whose projective splitting has kernel $K$ with $K=C_\beta^+K$, also vanishing by the least-degree argument; hence the Hilbert series is a finite Laurent polynomial times $\mathrm{gdim}\,C_\beta=(\beta)_q$. Symmetry of the tensor form is commutativity of the balanced tensor $P^\psi\otimes_RQ\cong Q^\psi\otimes_RP$ under the flip; the comparison form is the evaluation isomorphism $\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,R)\otimes_RQ\to\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,Q)$, $f\otimes v\mapsto(p\mapsto f(p)v)$, an isomorphism for shifted free $P$ and hence for all finite graded projective summands, twisted by $\psi$ on the first factor.

**Shifts and the two normalizations.** The total Hom-degree convention is that of [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]], so $h(P\{r\},Q\{s\})=q^{s-r}h(P,Q)$; no scalar conjugation of the tensor value is valid, and the rank-one values $(R(\alpha_i),R(\alpha_i))=1/(1-q_i^2)$ already show that the Hom form is not the plain scalar extension of the tensor form. The generator values follow from $P_i=R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]$, $P_i^\psi\otimes_{R(\alpha_i)}P_i\cong k[x_1]$ with $\deg x_1=2d_i$, and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$ because the two weight components are orthogonal. The cited projective/module Hom suppliers concern finite-dimensional algebras. Here the same shift and additivity formulas follow directly from homogeneous Hom and evaluation on finite shifted-free modules and summands; their finite-dimensional hypotheses are not applied to $R(\beta)$. The anti-involution $\psi$ is recorded explicitly because it fixes the sign of the shift in the Hom form. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Maximal KLR tails give a unique induction head and absolute simple modules
items.statement: Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; identify the nil-Hecke tail by matrix units, compute the maximal restriction through the Mackey filtration, then run the triangular basis argument.

1.1 (Nil-Hecke tail and its matrix units.) The constant-colour block $NH_r=R(r\alpha_i)$ acts on its polynomial column over $C_r=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]^{S_r}$. The Artin monomial basis and perfect symmetric-variable-linear trace of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] give integral matrix units and identify the full algebra with graded endomorphisms of that free rank-$r!$ column, hence with matrices over $C_r$ carrying the Artin degree shifts. Reducing the positive-degree central elementary symmetric functions to zero gives the graded matrix quotient over $k$; its column simple $L(i^r)$ is absolutely simple, and the divided idempotent cuts out a one-dimensional image. Its full-algebra polynomial-column graded projective cover has degree-zero endomorphism ring $k$, although its entire endomorphism ring is $C_r$. If $T$ is a finite-dimensional graded simple over $R(\mu)\otimes_kNH_r$, a positive-degree central operator has graded kernel and image. A nonzero such operator would therefore be invertible by graded simplicity, which is impossible on the finite nonzero degree support of $T$. Thus the positive tail center annihilates $T$, and it factors through $R(\mu)\otimes_k\operatorname{Mat}_{r!}(k)$ with the indicated shifts. Matrix units identify $T$ with $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ for a graded simple $R(\mu)$-module $N$, unique up to shift. This uses the augmentation matrix quotient for finite simples, not a false identification of the full nil-Hecke algebra with matrices over the ground field. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 (Maximal restriction.) Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional graded simple with $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ maximal. The finite-dimensional module $\Delta_i^rS$ is nonzero by the definition of $\epsilon_i$ and has a simple submodule; by step 1.1 it is of the form $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ for a graded simple $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$. If $N$ carried a word ending in $i$, then concatenating any nonzero nil-Hecke tail word would produce a nonzero vector in $S$ of tail $r+1$, contradicting maximality, so $\epsilon_i(N)=0$. By the left adjunction of [F2] the inclusion $N\boxtimes L(i^r)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^rS$ corresponds to a nonzero map $M:=\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))\to S$, which is surjective since $S$ is simple. In the Mackey filtration of $\Delta_i^rM$ every shuffle bringing $t>0$ colours $i$ from the first block into the final tail contains a factor $\Delta_i^tN$ and is zero; the only surviving filtration quotient is $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with zero crossing shift, so $\Delta_i^rM=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ exactly. This is a one-surviving-quotient computation, not a semisimplicity assumption. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 (Unique head and simplicity.) Every nonzero quotient $Q$ of $M$ has nonzero defining corner: if $eQ=0$ with $e=e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)$, then the composite $Ae\otimes_B(N\boxtimes L(i^r))\to M\to Q$ is zero by the tensor/Res adjunction, hence $Q=0$. The finite graded semisimple head of $M$ therefore has exactly one simple summand, occurring once, because its exact $e$-restriction is a quotient of the simple $eM=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; this head is $S$, and $eM\to eS$ is an isomorphism, so exactness gives $e\ker(M\to S)=0$ and every other composition factor of $M$ has smaller tail. Underlying and absolute simplicity of $S$: induct on the height of $\beta$. For positive height choose $i$ with $r>0$; by step 2.1 and induction $N$ and $L(i^r)$ are absolutely simple, so $eS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ has endomorphism ring $k$; if $U\le S$ is any ungraded submodule with $eU\ne0$, then $eU=eS$ and $U=S$ because $S$ is generated by $eS$; if $eU=0$ and $U\ne0$, filter $S$ by $F_dS=\bigoplus_{j\le d}S_j$ and $U$ by $F_dU=U\cap F_dS$. Every homogeneous algebra element of degree $a$ sends $F_dU$ into $F_{d+a}U$, so $\operatorname{gr}U$ embeds as a nonzero graded submodule of $\operatorname{gr}S=S$. Since $e$ has degree $0$ and annihilates $U$, it annihilates $\operatorname{gr}U$; graded simplicity gives $\operatorname{gr}U=S$, contradicting $eS\ne0$. Thus $S$ is simple as an ungraded module, and every $R$-endomorphism of $S$ is determined on $eS$, giving $\operatorname{End}_R(S)=k$. The finite-density matrix argument then shows absolute simplicity over every field: any $m$ linearly independent vectors can be sent to arbitrary targets by one algebra element, by induction on $m$ and the commutant $k$ clause, so the action realizes all $k$-linear matrices and remains simple after field extension. [step 2.1, F1, F3, algebra]

4.1 (Triangular divided-string basis.) Choose a cyclic order of the finite colour support and recursively strip maximal $i$-tails, producing for each simple shift orbit a finite tuple $Y_b$ of ordered divided powers; two simples with the same tuple agree by the unique-head recursion of step 3.1. Form $P(Y_b)$ from the reversed ordered normalized divided blocks. Its homogeneous Hom to $S_c$ is the corresponding product of divided idempotents acting on $S_c$; comparing tuples lexicographically, if $Y_b>Y_c$ at the first differing entry then the required tail exceeds the maximal tail of the successively stripped simple $S_c$, and the corner is zero. When the tuples agree, every maximal restriction is the simple tensor computed in step 2.1 and each nil-Hecke divided idempotent reduces the tail to one dimension, so by induction the diagonal Hom is a single Laurent monomial with coefficient $1$. Shifting each $S_b$ makes the diagonal $1$. The finite matrix is triangular over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ with diagonal $1$; Krull-Schmidt and the projective-cover/simple Hom pairing (now with $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ from step 3.1) identify it with the matrix expressing the projective classes in the cover basis, and successive integral triangular elimination proves that the selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ are an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; the whole family of divided words spans because the recursion covers every simple, while redundancy of non-selected words is allowed. This completes the integral surjectivity argument without a PBW rank or flat-family shortcut. [step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 (First-color version.) For maximal FIRST-color blocks use the defining idempotent $e(r\alpha_i,\mu)$ and $M=\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$ with $\epsilon_i^L(N)=0$; a simple submodule of the maximal first-block restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}S$ has the form $L(i^r)\boxtimes N$ by the same nil-Hecke matrix units of step 1.1, and any first-colour support of $N$ would extend the maximal first block, so it vanishes. In the Mackey restriction of $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}M$ every nontrivial shuffle bringing a positive number $t$ of $i$-colours from $N$ into the first block contains $\Delta_i^{(L,t)}N$ and is zero, so the sole uncrossed quotient is $L(i^r)\boxtimes N$ with shift $0$; the defining-corner generation and exact-head argument of steps 3.1 and 3.1 are unchanged. Thus the first-block assertions are proved directly, with no unsigned star-crystal preservation assumed. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.title: The KLR Grothendieck ring satisfies the divided-power quantum Serre relations
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $Af$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; build the induction algebra and restriction coalgebra, then the contracting homotopy for the Serre relation, then descend $\gamma$.

1.1 (Induction algebra and restriction coalgebra.) The induction product is associative and unital: the balanced identifications of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] for the two parenthesizations of three blocks are inverse degree-zero isomorphisms, and the unit is $[R(0)]=[k]$. For the block algebra $B$, the positive-center quotient is the tensor product of the two finite-dimensional graded quotients from [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Their simples are absolutely simple by [[lem-klr-maximal-tail-restriction-and-induction-have-a-unique-simple-head]], so their graded semisimple quotients are products of split graded matrix algebras. Tensoring these matrix blocks gives all simple shift orbits of $B$; tensor products of the factor projective covers cover them, by reducing their kernels and using the graded least-degree argument. Uniqueness of covers therefore identifies $K_0(B)$ with $K_0(R(\beta))\otimes_AK_0(R(\gamma))$. Restriction is coassociative with counit the weight-zero component, because iterated idempotent restriction multiplies the corresponding block idempotents, and the two orders of multiplication agree. To prove that $[\mathrm{Res}]$ respects the twisted multiplication, apply the Mackey filtration [F1] to the corner $e_{\beta,\gamma}Re_{\beta',\gamma'}$: PBW partitions its basis by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length, and multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms; the associated quotient is exactly the four-block restriction/induction bimodule shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives $[\mathrm{Res}](xy)=\sum q^{-(|y_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ with the twisted product, so $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism; no use of the second adjunction is needed. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 (Explicit Serre contraction.) Fix $i\ne j$, write $d=-a_{ij}$, $D=d+1$, $N=d+2$, and $t=[u^d]Q_{ij}\ne0$. For $0\le r\le D$, let $E_r$ be the product of the reflected nil-Hecke idempotents on the two $i$-blocks in $i^rji^{D-r}$, let $s_r=-d_i(\binom r2+\binom{D-r}2)$, and put $C_r=R E_r\{s_r\}$. Use right multiplication by $a_r=E_r\tau_{N-1}\cdots\tau_{r+1}E_{r+1}$ for $C_r\to C_{r+1}$ and by $b_r=E_{r+1}\tau_1\cdots\tau_{r+1}E_r$ in the reverse direction. Each string crosses $j$ once and respectively $D-r-1$ or $r$ equal-color pairs, so its degrees are $d_id-2d_i(D-r-1)$ and $d_id-2d_ir$. As $s_{r+1}-s_r=d_i(D-2r-1)$, both maps have degree zero between the shifted columns. The nil-Hecke identities $\tau_aE_r=0$ for equal-color crossings internal to its divided blocks and the braid moves give $a_{r-1}a_r=0$. At corner $r$, put $L_r=a_rb_r$, $R_r=b_{r-1}a_{r-1}$, with absent endpoint terms zero. Moving far crossings cancels the common strings in $L_r-R_r$; the remaining braid correction is the divided difference of $Q_{ij}$. For a monomial $u^av^b$ its correction is the sum of $a$ monomials of combined outer degree $a-1$, with the native minus sign. The $r-1$ left and $D-r-1$ right equal-color divided differences kill it unless $a\ge d$; homogeneity permits $a=d$ only when $b=0$, and permits no $a>d$. For $a=d$ exactly the staircase exponents $r-1,D-r-1$ survive, each evaluated by the nil-Hecke trace calculation of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]; transporting the variable order on the left block gives $L_r-R_r=(-1)^rtE_r$, including endpoints. Thus $h_r=(-1)^rt^{-1}b_r$ satisfies $a_rh_r+h_{r-1}a_{r-1}=E_r$ on every corner. These degree-zero maps contract the finite complex $(C_r,a_r)$ over every field and every (Q1)–(Q4) parameter. [step 1.1, algebra, construct]

3.1 (Alternating classes and the $a_{ij}=0$ case.) A bounded complex with $dh+hd=1$ is split contractible: choosing the successive splittings gives a contraction with $h^2=0$, and then $d+h$ is an isomorphism from even to odd part; hence the alternating sum of the classes of its terms vanishes, which is exactly $\sum_{a+b=D}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}][P_{j,1}][P_{i,b}]=0$, the displayed Serre relation. If $a_{ij}=0$ then the crossing $\tau$ of the two colours is invertible (its square is the nonzero constant $Q_{ij}$), and right multiplication by it gives a degree-zero isomorphism between the two corners, so $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{ij}]=[P_{ji}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 (Descent of $\gamma$.) First define $\gamma$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ from the presentation of the negative Serre half: [F3] identifies the Serre-presented rational negative half with the actual negative subalgebra, and the assignments $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$, extended multiplicatively and $q$-linearly, respect all Serre relations by step 3.1 and the commuting relation, so they define an algebra homomorphism $\gamma_{\mathbb Q}$ on the localization. Since the $A$-form is the $A$-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words [F2], and $[P_{i,1}]^n=[n]_i![P_{i,n}]$ by the nil-Hecke decomposition, so every rational divided power maps to $[P_{i,n}]$. These divided-word images lie in $K_0(R)$, which embeds in its rational scalar extension because its shift-orbit basis is free, the homomorphism restricts to the stated $A$-linear $\gamma$; the formula $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$ is multiplicativity of $\gamma$ together with the definition of $P_\theta$. Coproduct compatibility is the Mackey computation of step 1.1, and bar compatibility is the projective $^\#$ duality of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], which fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ and hence each word class. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve projective ranks. [step 1.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

items.title: The KLR Cartan pairing is the Lusztig-normalized half form
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], let $B_K$ be the normalized Lusztig-Kashiwara form on the negative half of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]] and put $B_L:=C_
u B_K$ on the weight component $
u$, $C_
u=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-
u_i}$, the Lusztig-normalized form of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]. Then for homogeneous $x,y\in Af_
u$ the Cartan pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] satisfies
$$(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)=C_
u\,B_K(x,y),$$
where $\gamma:Af	o K_0(R)$ is the algebra homomorphism of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Equivalently, the two bilinear forms are equal under the identification of divided-power classes; in particular the KLR pairing is $\mathbb Q(q)$-nondegenerate on each finite weight component $Af_
u\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)$ after extending scalars, and $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))'_{KLR}=B_L(\overline{x},y)$, where bar acts on the first input. On generators: $([P_i],[P_j])=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}=B_L(	heta_i,	heta_j)$ and $([P_{i,n}],[P_{i,n}])=B_L(	heta_i^{(n)},	heta_i^{(n)})=\prod_{a=1}^n(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; compare the two forms on a spanning set by the same recursive characterization, then upgrade with the supplier's nondegeneracy.

1.1 (Tensor adjunction.) Write $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes R(\gamma)$ and $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$. Reflection fixes each block and gives $(Ae\otimes_BX)^\psi=X^\psi\otimes_BeA$, with the same total grading. Thus $T(\operatorname{Ind}X,Y)=\mathrm{gdim}(X^\psi\otimes_BeY)=T_B(X,\operatorname{Res}Y)$. For $X=P\boxtimes Q$, the last tensor factorizes, giving the tensor-product form. Symmetry supplies the adjunction in the other variable. Pull this identity back through $\gamma$, using its coproduct compatibility from [F2]. The coefficient of $F_i\otimes z$ in $r(y)$ is $e_i'y$: on words this follows by deleting an $i$ and accumulating $q_i^{-a_{ij}}$ for each preceding letter in the twisted product, exactly the recursion of [F4]. Weight orthogonality therefore gives $T(\gamma(F_ix),\gamma(y))=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}T(\gamma(x),\gamma(e_i'y))$, with vacuum value $1$. [given, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

1.2 (Abstract side.) $B_K$ is characterized by (H), (N), (R) of [F3], and its normalized multiple $B_L=C_\nu B_K$ satisfies the generator value $B_L(\theta_i,\theta_j)=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and the recursion $B_L(F_iP,Q)=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}B_L(P,e_i'Q)$ by [F4]; the same recursion with the same base value determines every value on word monomials inductively, since peeling the first letter of the first argument and applying the recursion reduces the positive height by one. [given, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 (Comparison on monomials.) The KLR pairing and $B_L$ satisfy the same recursion and the same value at $1$: on the KLR side this is step 1.1 with $\gamma(F_i)=\gamma(\theta_i)=[P_{i,1}]=[P_i]$ and the identification of the restriction class with the coproduct; on the abstract side it is step 1.2. Induction on the height of the weight components therefore gives $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)$ on all divided-power monomials and hence on all of $Af$ by bilinearity, using that $\gamma$ is onto the classes of the divided words by [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Injectivity of $\gamma$ is not used: the equality is checked on the spanning monomials. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 (Nondegeneracy and generator values.) By [F5] the form $B_K$, hence the unit multiple $B_L$, is nondegenerate on each finite weight component, so the KLR tensor pairing is nondegenerate there as well; the Axiom of Choice enters only through this supplier, and the categorical comparison of steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 is choice-free. The Hom-form identity $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))'=B_L(\overline{x},y)$ follows from $h(P,Q)=T(P^\#,Q)$ of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] and $\gamma(\overline{x})=\gamma(x)^\#$ from [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]], clause (iii). For the rank-one divided power, $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ gives $([P_{i,n}],[P_{i,n}])=\prod_{a=1}^n(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$, matching $B_L(\theta_i^{(n)},\theta_i^{(n)})$ by the recursion of step 1.2; for $n=1$ this is the generator value already recorded. [step 2.1, F4, F5, algebra] ∎

items.title: The KLR category categorifies the negative quantum half
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $Af$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free $A$-rank of $Af_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; surjectivity by the triangular divided-string basis, injectivity by the preserved nondegenerate form, then compatibility.

1.1 (Surjectivity.) By [F1] the classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$ for a finite family of ordered divided-power words; each $Y_b$ is a word in divided powers of single colours, so its class equals $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})$ by multiplicativity of $\gamma$ and the definition of $P_\theta$. Hence every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is an $A$-linear combination of classes $[P_\theta]$ of divided-power projectives, and $\gamma$ is onto. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 (Injectivity.) Suppose $\gamma(x)=0$ for some $x\in Af_\nu$. By [F2] and [F3], for every $y$ in the same weight component one has $B_L(x,y)=(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))=0$; since $B_L$ is a unit multiple of the nondegenerate form $B_K$ on the finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q(q)$-space $Af_\nu\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)$, this forces $x=0$. The categorical and form-comparison steps of [F2] are choice-free; the Axiom of Choice is inherited only through the nondegeneracy supplier [F3]. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 (Compatibility and ranks.) The intertwining of multiplications is multiplicativity of $\gamma$ together with the induction formula of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]; the intertwining of comultiplications is the Mackey comparison of [[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]] against the coproduct $r$ of the negative half; the bar compatibility is $P_{i,n}^\#=P_{i,n}$ for the normalized divided projectives of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], and form preservation is [F2]. Since $\gamma$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules by steps 1.1 and 2.1, the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals that of $Af_\beta$; the finite free basis supplied by [F1] transfers through $\gamma$ to a finite free basis of $Af_\beta$, and the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself is not compared with $f_\beta$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: Self-dual KLR projectives have positive first-block divided-string leading terms
items.statement:
For any graded KLR datum in this page and any field $k$, each finite-dimensional graded simple shift orbit has a unique representative $S_b$ self-dual for $D(M)_d=\operatorname{Hom}_k(M_{-d},k)$ with action $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. Its projective cover $P_b$, normalized by $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P_b,S_b)=k$, satisfies $P_b^\#=P_b$ for $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,R)^\psi$. These are unique normalizations. Induction of two self-dual finite projectives is self-dual. If $\epsilon_i^L(S_b)=r>0$ and $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}S_b=L(i^r)\boxtimes S_a$ with $\epsilon_i^L(S_a)=0$, normalized as above, then
$$[P_{i,r}][P_a]=[P_b]+\sum_{\epsilon_i^L(S_c)>r}m_c(q)[P_c],$$
with $m_c\in\mathbb{N}[q,q^{-1}]$ each invariant under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$. Under $\gamma$ the integral LEFT divided-string ideal $I_{(i,\ge n)}=\sum_{r\ge n}F_i^{(r)}U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of $[P_b]$ with $\epsilon_i^L(S_b)\ge n$. Consequently, if the normalized projective classes are known to be a SIGNED lower-global set, this leading coefficient $1$ identifies them with the POSITIVE lower-global set using the general adapted right-string recursion; no finite-ADE canonical-comparison theorem is needed. For the conclusions compared with the quantum half and the conditional lower-global/LEFT-string recursion, carry the inherited Axiom of Choice of those quantum suppliers; the generic finite module duality/parity/Frobenius arguments themselves are choice-free.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct; normalize dualities by word characters, compute the first-block expansion, then compare with the integral string ideals and the global recursion.

1.1 (Self-dual simples.) The maximal-tail supplier [F1] gives a triangular divided-idempotent/simple Hom matrix with diagonal $1$ over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, which remains invertible at $q=1$. Ordinary dimensions of divided-word corners are determined by ordinary word dimensions: in each constant-colour block the nil-Hecke matrix presentation makes the polynomial column simple of rank $r!$ and the divided idempotent a rank-one matrix projection, so $\dim(e_{	ext{div}}M)=\dim(e_{	ext{expanded}}M)/\prod_r r!$ for every finite module $M$, including nonsemisimple central quotients. The vector duality $D(M)_d=\operatorname{Hom}_k(M_{-d},k)$ preserves simple modules and fixes ordinary word dimensions because $\psi$ fixes the word idempotents, so $DS\cong S\{s\}$ for some integer $s$. 3.1 (Self-dual covers and induction.) For a finite projective $P$ and finite module $M$, evaluation gives $\operatorname{Hom}(P^\#,DM)=D\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)$ with ordinary homogeneous degrees: verify on $P=Re(
u)\{a\}$, where both sides are the dual of the finite-dimensional space $e(

The duality $^\#$ is an involution on finite projectives, so $P_b^\#$ is the same normalized indecomposable projective cover of $DS_b=S_b$, giving $P_b^\#=P_b$; a nonzero projective is bounded below, so the normalization is unique. If $M$ is a finite projective over the separated block algebra $B$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Re\otimes_BM,R)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,eR)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,B)\otimes_BeR$ by evaluation on finite free modules and summands, and twisting by $\psi$ identifies this with $Re\otimes_BM^\#$ without reversing the horizontal block order; for $M=P_a oxtimes P_{i,r}$ this proves that $\mathrm{Ind}M$ is self-dual. Restriction commutes with $D$ because $\psi$ fixes the defining block idempotent, so the maximal FIRST-block restriction of the normalized $S_b$ is exactly the normalized $L(i^r) oxtimes S_a$ with no residual shift: that tensor is $D$-self-dual and any extra shift would contradict finite support. [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 (Leading coefficient $1$.) Use the exact tensor/Res adjunction of [[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]] and the maximal-tail lemma [F1] to compute $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i,r} oxtimes P_a),S_c)$: it vanishes if $\epsilon_i^L(S_c)<r$; if $\epsilon_i^L(S_c)=r$, the maximal restriction is $L(i^r) oxtimes S_{a'}$ and the Hom is zero unless $a'=a$, when it is exactly $k$ in degree $0$; the unique-head lemma makes $c=b$ in that case. Since Hom from a projective detects the multiplicity polynomial of each summand in the decomposition, the induced projective has exactly $[P_b]$ with coefficient $1$ at tail $r$ and all other summands at strictly higher tail, giving the displayed expansion. Self-duality of the induction and of each normalized projective forces every multiplicity polynomial to be bar invariant, and finite decompositions give nonnegative coefficients. [step 3.1, F1, F2, algebra]

5.1 (Integral string ideals.) For every $n$, induction with a divided block of length $r\ge n$ has no summands of tail $<n$ by the same Hom computation of step 4.1, so $\gamma(I_{(i,\ge n)})$ is contained in the span of the corresponding covers. Conversely descend on the finite possible tail $r$ (bounded by $ eta_i$): the coefficient-$1$ expansion expresses every $[P_b]$ of tail $r$ as $[P_{i,r}][P_a]$ minus classes of strictly higher tail, which lie in $I_{(i,\ge r)}$ already; this proves the reverse inclusion integrally, using the sum of all divided images and not a Gaussian-unit identification with a single ordinary power ideal. [step 4.1, F3, algebra]

6.1 (Signs.) Suppose $[P_b]=\gamma(\mathrm{sign}_b\,G(b'))$ has been established by a separate norm/geometric argument. The ideal equality of step 5.1 and the adapted LEFT-string lower-global basis [F4] identify the tail partitions of these signed vectors with the LEFT string partitions; at the exact LEFT-string quotient the lower-global recursion has coefficient $+1$ for $F_i^{(r)}G(a')$ when $a'$ has LEFT string $0$. Induction on root height fixes $\mathrm{sign}_a=+1$, and comparing the projective coefficient-$1$ expansion with this quotient fixes $\mathrm{sign}_b=+1$; the unit/vacuum starts the induction. The reversal supplier used elsewhere promises only signed star preservation, so an unsigned right recursion is deliberately not inferred here. The Axiom of Choice enters only through the inherited quantum-half/global suppliers [F4] and [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); no additional simultaneous module-basis choice is used, and the finite duality, parity, Frobenius and first-block multiplicity arguments above are choice-free. [step 5.1, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

items.statement: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every $i$, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.

2.2 (Graded Yoneda.) Use the shifted opposite-composition product of [F3] and define $Y_T=\operatorname{Ext}_G^ ullet(L,T)$ as a graded left $R$-module: for homogeneous $a:L	o L[n]$ and $y:L	o T[m]$, set $a\cdot y=y[n]\circ a$, so $(a*b)\cdot y=a\cdot(b\cdot y)$. On $T=L$ this is the regular left module. A homogeneous map $f:T	o U[t]$ acts by postcomposition $y\mapsto f[m]\circ y$ of degree $t$. For $T=U=L$ every graded $R$-linear map $R	o R$ is right multiplication by its value at $1$, hence is induced uniquely by the corresponding $f$; extend this identification to finite sums and shifts and then to idempotent summands. Since the actual category is idempotent complete and all finite graded projectives are summands of finite sums of shifts of $R$, this gives a fully faithful equivalence from the additive category generated by shifts of $L$ onto finite graded projectives, with $\operatorname{End}_R^ ullet(Y_T)\cong\operatorname{Ext}_G^ ullet(T,T)$ using ordinary categorical composition on both endomorphism rings. [F3, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (Indecomposables and scalar degree zero.) Each simple perverse summand $T$ in step 2.1 belongs to that additive category up to shift. By [F4] and step 2.2 its projective $Y_T$ has no negative-degree endomorphisms and its degree-zero endomorphism ring is a division algebra, hence it is graded indecomposable. These exhaust the indecomposable projective shift orbits: every projective is a summand of a finite sum of the $Y_T$ and their shifts, and [F5] gives the finite graded Krull–Schmidt decomposition. Distinct simple perverse objects yield distinct orbits, since full faithfulness would otherwise give $T\cong U[t]$, and perverse concentration forces $t=0$. Finally the simple head $S$ of $Y_T$ has $\operatorname{End}_R^0(S)=k$ by [F5]. Every degree-zero endomorphism preserves the unique maximal graded submodule, so descent to the head is a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\operatorname{End}_R^0(Y_T)	o k$; its kernel is zero because its source is a division algebra, and its image contains all scalars, so $\operatorname{End}_R^0(Y_T)=k$. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]


4.1 (Self-dual normalization, norm one and signed globalization.) By [F1] every indecomposable projective shift orbit has a unique $^\#$ self-dual representative $P_b$; put $x_b=\gamma^{-1}[P_b]$, which is integral and bar fixed. The exact Hom/tensor comparison for a self-dual $P$ gives $B_L(x_b,x_b)=h(P_b,P_b)$, a nonnegative integer power series in $q$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$, since the geometric nonnegative-End property is unchanged by grading shifts. Dividing by $C_ eta$ (which is $1$ modulo $q$) gives a value $B_K(x_b,x_b)$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ with integer coefficients, so the general half norm criterion places $x_b$ in the $q^0$ crystal lattice; being bar fixed, it also lies in the actual bar chart, and the integral balanced globalization writes $x_b$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of lower global vectors. Their residue Gram matrix is the identity, so norm residue $1$ forces the sum of coefficient squares to be $1$: $x_b$ is exactly plus or minus one lower global vector. Distinct projective shift orbits are independent and have the same finite weight cardinality as the global basis by the integral $K_0$ isomorphism, so they exhaust this signed set. [step 3.1, F1, F2, algebra]

5.1 (Positivity and the based quotient.) The positive divided-string leading-term supplier [F2] removes every minus sign using its integral LEFT-string ideal equality, its coefficient-$1$ projective adjunction expansion, and the general adapted LEFT global recursion (carried with its inherited Axiom of Choice, [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); batch 8's finite-ADE canonical-comparison item is not used. Consequently the sign in step 4.1 is $+1$, giving $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for every lower global vector $G(b)$ and establishing the bijection of the statement. The compatibility with the based quotient is the general zero/survival projection theorem of the QG-5 machinery. [step 4.1, F2, algebra] ∎

**Proof technique:** direct; read off the two-strand PBW basis and check both parameter cases.

1.1 (Two-strand basis and dimension.) In weight $\alpha_i+\alpha_j$ the sequences are $ij$ and $ji$, and $S_2=\{1,s_1\}$, so the PBW basis [F3] consists of the four families $x_1^ax_2^be(ij)$, $x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1e(ij)$, $x_1^ax_2^be(ji)$, $x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1e(ji)$, which is rank $4$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$; grouping by idempotent gives rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]e(ij)\oplus k[x_1,x_2]e(ji)$. The graded dimension is the two geometric series for the dots in degrees $2d_i,2d_j$ in each corner plus the crossing contributions: in the $ij$-corner, $\tau_1e(ij)$ has degree $-b_{ij}$, and in the $ji$-corner $\tau_1e(ji)$ has degree $-b_{ji}=-b_{ij}$, giving $\frac{1+q^{-b_{ij}}}{(1-q^{2d_i})(1-q^{2d_j})}$ in each corner, total $\frac{2(1+q^{-b_{ij}})}{(1-q^{2d_i})(1-q^{2d_j})}$. [given, F3, algebra]

1.2 (Case $a_{ij}=0$.) Here $Q_{ij}=1$ is a nonzero constant with $Q_{ji}=1$, so [F1] gives $\tau_1^2e(ij)=e(ij)$ and $\tau_1^2e(ji)=e(ji)$, i.e. $\tau_1^2=e(ij)+e(ji)$, and the dot slides $\tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1$, $\tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1$ (distinct colours). Right multiplication by $\tau_1$ is an isomorphism of graded left modules $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)e(ij)\to R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)e(ji)$ with inverse right multiplication by $\tau_1$ on the other side: both composites are $\tau_1^2=\mathrm{id}$ on the respective corners, and the map is degree-zero because $\deg\tau_1=-b_{ij}=0$. Hence $[P_{ij}]=[R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)e(ij)]=[R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)e(ji)]=[P_{ji}]$ in $K_0(R)$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 (Case $a_{ij}=-1$.) With $P_{ij}=u+v$, $P_{ji}=1$ we have $P_{ij}(u,v)P_{ji}(v,u)=(u+v)\cdot1=Q_{ij}(u,v)$, a valid factorization with both factors nonzero, so [F2] applies: $\tau_1(fe(ij))=(x_1+x_2)f(x_2,x_1)e(ji)$ and $\tau_1(fe(ji))=1\cdot f(x_2,x_1)e(ij)$. Applying twice, $\tau_1^2(fe(ij))=(x_1+x_2)f$ and $\tau_1^2(fe(ji))=(x_1+x_2)f$, so $\tau_1^2e(\nu)=Q_{\nu_1\nu_2}(x_1,x_2)e(\nu)$ on both summands, as required by [F1]. The freeness statements are step 1.1. For the Serre relation, apply [F4] with $a_{ij}=-1$: the sum runs over $a+b=2$ with signs $+,-,+$, i.e. $[P_{i,2}][P_j]-[P_{i,1}][P_j][P_{i,1}]+[P_j][P_{i,2}]=0$, which in the divided-word notation is $[P_{i(2)j}]-[P_{iji}]+[P_{ji(2)}]=0$, i.e. $[P_{iji}]=[P_{i(2)j}]+[P_{ji(2)}]$. [step 1.1, F2, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: The KLR algebras in root degrees $\alpha_i$ and $2\alpha_i$
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix $i\in I$.
(a) In weight $\alpha_i$ there is one sequence, and $R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]e(i)$: the only relations are that $x_1$ is central, so $\{x_1^a\}_{a\ge0}$ is a $k$-basis, $\deg x_1=2d_i$, and $\mathrm{gdim}\,R(\alpha_i)=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$. The algebra is commutative; up to shift its unique graded simple module is $k$ with $x_1$ acting by $0$, $R(\alpha_i)$ is the projective cover of that simple, and $[R(\alpha_i)]=[P_{i,1}]$ with $([P_{i,1}],[P_{i,1}])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$.
(b) In weight $2\alpha_i$ one has $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$, the nil Hecke algebra of rank $2$, with $k$-basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,\ x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}_{a,b\ge0}$, free of rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$, and relations (in the normalization of relation (6) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]])
$$\tau_1^2=0,\qquad \tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii),\qquad \tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1-e(ii).$$
Its graded dimension is $\dfrac{1+q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$, and the element $e_{i,2}=x_1\tau_1$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ with $P_{i,2}=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ an indecomposable projective of class $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ in $K_0(R)$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct computation in the two lowest weights.

1.1 (a) In weight $\alpha_i$ the only sequence is $(i)$, and there are no crossings, so the presentation reduces to the single generator $x_1$ with relation (2) $x_1e(i)=e(i)x_1$; hence $R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]e(i)$ with basis $\{x_1^a\}$, $\deg x_1=2d_i$ by [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], and $\mathrm{gdim}R(\alpha_i)=\sum_{a\ge0}q^{2d_ia}=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$. A graded simple is cyclic and bounded below; the positive-degree central $x_1$ cannot act bijectively on it, so simplicity forces $x_1S=0$. Thus its unique graded simple is $k=R(\alpha_i)/(x_1)$ up to shift; $R(\alpha_i)$ is free of rank one over itself, hence projective, indecomposable (its endomorphism ring is $k[x_1]$, whose only idempotents are $0,1$), and its quotient onto $k$ is a graded projective cover: if a graded submodule $U$ satisfies $U+(x_1)=R$, comparison in degree zero gives $1\in U$, hence $U=R$; the pairing value is the normalization of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]: $P_i^\psi\otimes_{R(\alpha_i)}P_i\cong k[x_1]$ as a graded space. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

1.2 (b) In weight $2\alpha_i$ there is one sequence $(ii)$ and one crossing $\tau_1$, with relations (4) and (6) specialized to $Q_{ii}=0$: $\tau_1^2=0$ and, on the equal-colour component, $\tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii)$, $\tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1-e(ii)$. The PBW basis [F1] is $\{x_1^ax_2^b,\ x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}_{a,b\ge0}$, which is free of rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$; the graded dimension is the sum of the two geometric series $\frac1{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}+\frac{q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}=\frac{1+q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$ because $\tau_1$ has degree $-b_{ii}=-2d_i$. For the idempotent: $e_{i,2}^2=x_1\tau_1x_1\tau_1=x_1(x_2\tau_1+e(ii))\tau_1=x_1x_2\tau_1^2+x_1\tau_1=x_1\tau_1=e_{i,2}$ using $\tau_1^2=0$, and $e_{i,2}\ne0$ by the PBW basis; its degree is $2d_i+(-2d_i)=0$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 (b, continued) By [F2] with $n=2$ the element $e_{i,2}=x_1\tau_1$ is the divided-power idempotent, $P_{i,2}=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift, and $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$; the shift here is $-\binom22d_i=-d_i$. [step 1.2, F2, algebra] ∎
